chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from one of his companions from Aban ibn Uthman from one of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the child, when he becomes a youth, so he chooses Christianity, and one of his parents is a Christian, or they are both Muslims. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would not be left, but he would be whipped upon Islam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mature child who chooses Christianity when one parent is Christian?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the penalty for a child who reaches maturity (bulugh) and explicitly chooses Christianity, even if one parent is Christian or both are Muslim. The ruling indicates that the child is not merely left to their choice but is compelled to embrace Islam through physical discipline (whipping), reflecting the Shia view of apostasy as a capital offense requiring enforcement. This highlights the distinction between the child's initial upbringing and their conscious adult choice to leave the faith.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else from his companions, from Aban Bin Usman, from one of his companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the child, when he becomes a youth, so he chooses the Christianity, and one of his parents is a Christian, or they are both Muslims. He<sup>asws</sup> Said: ‘He would not be left, but he would be whipped upon Al-Islam’.
